title: Bending of Light: The Critical Angle
markdown:
Light traveling from a denser medium into a less dense medium bends (refracts) at the boundary. The **critical angle** determines whether the light escapes or reflects back.

{{viz:0}}

### Three Cases

1. **Angle of Incidence < Critical Angle** — The light ray crosses the boundary and refracts into the less dense medium, bending away from the normal.
2. **Angle of Incidence = Critical Angle** — The refracted ray travels exactly along the boundary between the two media.
3. **Angle of Incidence > Critical Angle** — **Total internal reflection** occurs: the light does not cross the boundary and instead reflects back into the denser medium.

> **Why it matters for fiber optics**: Optical fiber is designed so that light entering the core always hits the core/cladding boundary at an angle *greater* than the critical angle, ensuring total internal reflection and keeping the light trapped inside the core as it travels the length of the cable.
